LESSON: READING 12.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: COMPREHENSION STRATEGIES

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.2: Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to summarise information from a text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify clues in the passage from which conclusions can be drawn
2. apply the skills of making inferences and drawing conclusions in independent reading

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 12.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: COMPREHENSION STRATEGIES
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 12.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: COMPREHENSION STRATEGIES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify clues in the passage from which conclusions can be drawn

What this means
In this part you learn to identify clues in the passage from which conclusions can be drawn. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify clues in the passage from which conclusions can be drawn.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify clues in the passage from which conclusions can be drawn. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply the skills of making inferences and drawing conclusions in independent reading

What this means
In this part you learn to apply the skills of making inferences and drawing conclusions in independent reading. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply the skills of making inferences and drawing conclusions in independent reading.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply the skills of making inferences and drawing conclusions in independent reading. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify clues in the passage from which conclusions can be drawn)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies to a partner. (skill: apply the skills of making inferences and drawing conclusions in independent reading)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify clues in the passage from which conclusions can be drawn.
3. Practise this skill: apply the skills of making inferences and drawing conclusions in independent reading.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to summarise information from a text?
2. How can one draw conclusions from a text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify clues in the passage from which conclusions can be drawn.
5. Be able to: apply the skills of making inferences and drawing conclusions in independent reading.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
